topics.label: Introduction to the initiation and resolution of inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer opens the session by outlining how previously introduced immune cells and molecules combine to drive and resolve inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Pattern recognition receptors and danger sensing pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the innate immune system detects danger through pathogen- and damage-associated molecular patterns acting on cell-surface and intracellular pattern recognition receptors.

topics.label: Cellular and vascular events in acute and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sentinel cells trigger leukocyte recruitment into inflamed tissues and how excessive inflammatory signaling can escalate to systemic pathology.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic responses
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the mechanisms responsible for terminating inflammation, repairing injured tissue, and managing persistent insults through chronic inflammation and granuloma formation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation and announces the topic of the following lecture.
